flavor_text.one_line: A chaotic animist chorus that celebrates shedding old selves so the spirit may return fiercer and freer.
flavor_text.one_paragraph: The Many-Shed Chorus teaches that life is a sequence of masks, skins, and names to be worn, broken, and reborn. Its shamans bargain with a host of wild spirits, some nurturing and some cruel, and insist that only the dead who refuse to fade entirely have understood how precious change truly is. Their rites are sung on high branches, in drowned clearings, and beneath split moons, where revelation arrives through dance, trance, and ecstatic fear.
flavor_text.creation_myth_summary: The first spirit split the moon with antlers and scattered its silver skins across the void; every world and body is one of those cast-off skins learning to live.
flavor_text.moral_code_summary: Break false chains, seize beauty before it withers, honor the returning dead, and defy every power that would nail the soul into one obedient form.
